headline: Medium prompt-injection and cascading-error risks from ComfyUI outputs feeding plano’s broad-egress gateway; no direct shared-channel evidence, so interaction is inferred.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ComfyUI is offline and has no clipboard/MCP/shared-channel surface, while plano exposes an OpenAI-compatible chat endpoint with broad egress. No direct bridge is documented, so prompt injection is only plausible if an operator manually pipes ComfyUI text into plano.
conditions: IF an operator copies ComfyUI-generated text into plano prompts or config
IF a shared file or message queue is added between ComfyUI and plano
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Disable any manual copy-paste workflow for untrusted text
Add a review step before plano consumes ComfyUI output
Use a fixed prompt template that strips instructions
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between systems

B_data_leakage.rationale: ComfyUI touches local media/model files and can run fully offline; plano touches logs/metrics and has broad network egress. The pair does not show a shared filesystem or authenticated principal, so leakage is limited to operator-mediated transfer rather than default cross-agent exposure.
conditions: IF the operator places sensitive images or prompts into both agents
IF a shared workspace or synced folder is introduced
mitigations: Store sensitive assets outside any shared folder
Use separate OS accounts for each agent
Turn off automatic log export in plano
Review ComfyUI workflow inputs before reuse
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ComfyUI cannot write files, modify git, or spawn subprocesses, and supports no multiple instances; plano also lacks filesystem write and subprocess capabilities. With no overlapping mutable resource writes documented, direct capability conflict is unlikely.
conditions: IF either agent is later granted write access to the same directory
IF an orchestrator adds shared mutable state or locking-free coordination
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only where possible
Avoid shared git or database state
Run them under separate service accounts
Document any future write scopes before enabling them
requires-engineering: add locking around shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: ComfyUI can generate workflows, images, and model artifacts that plano could ingest as agentic signals or logs. plano’s gateway role makes it plausible it will route or act on upstream content, so A-to-B propagation exists even without direct evidence of verification failure.
conditions: IF plano consumes ComfyUI-produced text or metadata as routing input
IF no human or automated verification step checks ComfyUI outputs before plano acts
mitigations: Require explicit validation before plano uses upstream outputs
Separate generation from routing responsibilities
Add schema checks on any ComfyUI-derived payload
Log and review rejected upstream artifacts
requires-engineering: implement provenance-aware gating

E_compliance.rationale: ComfyUI is documented as fully offline and touches local media/model data, while plano has broad egress and logs/metrics handling. No residency or certification mismatch is documented, so compliance risk is limited to accidental operator routing of regulated data into plano.
conditions: IF regulated images or prompts are sent from ComfyUI into plano
IF plano logs contain data classes subject to stricter retention or residency rules
mitigations: Do not route regulated data into plano
Set short log retention in plano
Use redaction for prompts and traces
Confirm residency requirements before deployment
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for data classes
